title: Constructing new permutation polynomials by the AGW Criterion
authors: Qian Liu, Liwei Fang, Zhengbang Zha, and Jing Zhang
abstract: In this paper, we propose several classes of permutation polynomials having the form $\sum\limits_i(x^{2^m}+x+\delta)^{s_i}+ax$ for $i=1$ or $i=2$, where the exponent $s_i$ satisfies $s_i\equiv 2^j\pmod{2^m+1}$ or $s_i \equiv 2^j\pmod{2^m-1}$ for some different integers $j$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_{2^m}^*$ and $\delta\in \mathbb{F}_{2^{2m}}$. More precisely, by applying the AGW criterion and determining the number of solutions to certain equations over $\mathbb{F}_{2^{2m}}$, several classes of permutation polynomials of the form $(x^{2^m}+x+\delta)^s+ax$ over $\mathbb{F}_{2^{2m}}$ are presented. In addition, we construct some classes of permutation polynomials of the form $(x^{2^m}+x+\delta)^{s_1}+(x^{2^m}+x+\delta)^{s_2}+ax$ over $\mathbb{F}_{2^{2m}}$. Our results generalize some known constructions of permutation polynomials. Finally, we demonstrate that the permutation polynomials proposed in this paper are not quasi-multiplicative equivalent to known ones.

1        Introduction
    Let Fq denote the finite field with q elements, where q is a power of a prime p. Let F∗q denote
the multiplicative group of Fq . A polynomial f (x) ∈ Fq [x] is called a permutation polynomial (PP)
if the mapping x 7→ f (x) from Fq into itself is bijective. Furthermore, we call f (x) a complete
permutation polynomial (CPP) if both f (x) and f (x) + x are permutations of Fq . PPs have been
widely employed in cryptography [5, 18, 37], combinatorial design theory [4], coding theory [9], and
other areas of mathematics and engineering [8, 14, 16, 21, 24, 30]. In general, constructing PPs
over finite fields has been a prominent research topic in recent decades.
